NASB.1: When Israel [was] a youth I loved him, And out of Egypt I called My son.
NASB.2: The more they called them, The more they went from them; They kept sacrificing to the Baals And burning incense to idols.
NASB.3: Yet it is I who taught Ephraim to walk, I took them in My arms; But they did not know that I healed them.
NASB.4: I led them with cords of a man, with bonds of love, And I became to them as one who lifts the yoke from their jaws; And I bent down [and] fed them.
NASB.5: They will not return to the land of Egypt; But Assyria-- he will be their king Because they refused to return [to Me].
NASB.6: The sword will whirl against their cities, And will demolish their gate bars And consume [them] because of their counsels.
NASB.7: So My people are bent on turning from Me. Though they call them to [the One] on high, None at all exalts [Him].
NASB.8: How can I give you up, O Ephraim? How can I surrender you, O Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned over within Me, All My compassions are kindled.
NASB.9: I will not execute My fierce anger; I will not destroy Ephraim again. For I am God and not man, the Holy One in your midst, And I will not come in wrath.
NASB.10: They will walk after the LORD, He will roar like a lion; Indeed He will roar And [His] sons will come trembling from the west.
NASB.11: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt And like doves from the land of Assyria; And I will settle them in their houses, declares the LORD.
NASB.12: Ephraim surrounds Me with lies And the house of Israel with deceit; Judah is also unruly against God, Even against the Holy One who is faithful.

NKJV.1: “When Israel was a child, I loved him, And out of Egypt I called My son.
NKJV.2: As they called them, So they went from them; They sacrificed to the Baals, And burned incense to carved images.
NKJV.3: “I  taught Ephraim to walk, Taking them by their arms; But they did not know that I healed them.
NKJV.4: I drew them with gentle cords, With bands of love, And I was to them as those who take the yoke from their neck. I stooped and fed them.
NKJV.5: “He shall not return to the land of Egypt; But the Assyrian shall be his king, Because they refused to repent.
NKJV.6: And the sword shall slash in his cities, Devour his districts, And consume them, Because of their own counsels.
NKJV.7: My people are bent on backsliding from Me. Though they call to the Most High, None at all exalt Him.
NKJV.8: “How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I set you like Zeboiim? My heart churns within Me; My sympathy is stirred.
NKJV.9: I will not execute the fierceness of My anger; I will not again destroy Ephraim. For I am God, and not man, The Holy One in your midst; And I will not come with terror.
NKJV.10: “They shall walk after the LORD. He will roar like a lion. When He roars, Then His sons shall come trembling from the west;
NKJV.11: They shall come trembling like a bird from Egypt,  Like a dove from the land of Assyria.  And I will let them dwell in their houses,” Says the LORD.
NKJV.12: “Ephraim has encircled Me with lies, And the house of Israel with deceit; But Judah still walks with God, Even with the Holy One who is faithful.

ESV.1: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
ESV.2: The more they were called, the more they went away; they kept sacrificing to the Baals and burning offerings to idols.
ESV.3: Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk; I took them up by their arms, but they did not know that I healed them.
ESV.4: I led them with cords of kindness,  with the bands of love, and I became to them as one who eases the yoke on their jaws, and I bent down to them and fed them.
ESV.5: They shall not  return to the land of Egypt, but Assyria shall be their king, because they have refused to return to me.
ESV.6: The sword shall rage against their cities, consume the bars of their gates, and devour them because of their own counsels.
ESV.7: My people are bent on turning away from me, and though they call out to the Most High, he shall not raise them up at all.
ESV.8: How can I give you up, O Ephraim? How can I hand you over, O Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender.
ESV.9: I will not execute my burning anger; I will not again destroy Ephraim; for I am God and not a man, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not come in wrath.
ESV.10: They shall go after the LORD; he will roar like a lion; when he roars, his children shall come trembling from the west;
ESV.11: they shall come trembling like birds from Egypt, and like doves from the land of Assyria, and I will return them to their homes, declares the LORD.
ESV.12: Ephraim has surrounded me with lies, and the house of Israel with deceit, but Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.

AMP.1:
When Israel was a child [a young nation], I loved him,
And I called My son out of Egypt.
AMP.2:
The more they [the prophets] called them [to repentance and obedience],
The more they went away from them;
They kept sacrificing to the Baals
And burning incense to the carved images.
AMP.3:
Yet it is I who taught Ephraim to walk,
Taking them in My arms [nurturing the young nation];
But they did not know that I healed them.
AMP.4:
I led them gently with cords of a man, with bonds of love [guiding them],
And I was to them as one who lifts up and eases the yoke [of the law] over their jaws;
And I bent down to them and fed them.
AMP.5:
They will not return to the land of Egypt,
But Assyria will be their king [bringing them into captivity]
Because they refused to return to Me.
AMP.6:
The sword will whirl against and fall on their cities,
And will demolish the bars of their gates and fortifications
And will consume them because of their counsels.
AMP.7:
My people are bent on turning from Me;
Though the prophets call them to the One on high,
None at all exalts Him.
AMP.8:
How can I give you up, O Ephraim?
How can I surrender you, O Israel?
How can I make you like Admah?
How can I treat you like Zeboiim?
My heart recoils within Me;
All My compassions are kindled together [for My nation of Israel].
AMP.9:
I will not execute the fierceness of My anger;
I will not return to Ephraim to destroy him again.
For I am God and not man, the Holy One in your midst [who will not revoke My covenant],
And I will not come in wrath or enter the city [in judgment].
AMP.10:
They will walk after the LORD [in obedience and worship],
Who will roar like a lion;
He will roar [summoning them]
And His sons will come trembling from the west.
AMP.11:
They will come trembling and hurriedly like birds from Egypt
And like doves from the land of Assyria;
And I will settle them in their houses [in the land of their inheritance], declares the LORD.
AMP.12:
Ephraim surrounds Me with lies
And the house of Israel with deceit;
Judah is also unruly against God,
Even against the faithful Holy One.

NLT.1:
“When Israel was a child, I loved him,
and I called my son out of Egypt.
NLT.2:
But the more I called to him,
the farther he moved from me,
offering sacrifices to the images of Baal
and burning incense to idols.
NLT.3:
I myself taught Israel how to walk,
leading him along by the hand.
But he doesn’t know or even care
that it was I who took care of him.
NLT.4:
I led Israel along
with my ropes of kindness and love.
I lifted the yoke from his neck,
and I myself stooped to feed him.
NLT.5:
“But since my people refuse to return to me,
they will return to Egypt
and will be forced to serve Assyria.
NLT.6:
War will swirl through their cities;
their enemies will crash through their gates.
They will destroy them,
trapping them in their own evil plans.
NLT.7:
For my people are determined to desert me.
They call me the Most High,
but they don’t truly honor me.
NLT.8:
“Oh, how can I give you up, Israel?
How can I let you go?
How can I destroy you like Admah
or demolish you like Zeboiim?
My heart is torn within me,
and my compassion overflows.
NLT.9:
No, I will not unleash my fierce anger.
I will not completely destroy Israel,
for I am God and not a mere mortal.
I am the Holy One living among you,
and I will not come to destroy.
NLT.10:
For someday the people will follow me.
I, the LORD, will roar like a lion.
And when I roar,
my people will return trembling from the west.
NLT.11:
Like a flock of birds, they will come from Egypt.
Trembling like doves, they will return from Assyria.
And I will bring them home again,”
says the LORD.
NLT.12:
Israel surrounds me with lies and deceit,
but Judah still obeys God
and is faithful to the Holy One.

WEB.1: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
WEB.2: They called to them, so they went from them. They sacrificed to the Baals, and burned incense to engraved images.
WEB.3: Yet I taught Ephraim to walk. I took them by his arms; but they didn’t know that I healed them.
WEB.4: I drew them with cords of a man, with ties of love; and I was to them like those who lift up the yoke on their necks; and I bent down to him and I fed him.
WEB.5: “They won’t return into the land of Egypt; but the Assyrian will be their king, because they refused to repent.
WEB.6: The sword will fall on their cities, and will destroy the bars of their gates, and will put an end to their plans.
WEB.7: My people are determined to turn from me. Though they call to the Most High, he certainly won’t exalt them.
WEB.8: “How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I make you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned within me, my compassion is aroused.

MSG.1:
"When Israel was only a child, I loved him.
I called out, 'My son!'—called him out of Egypt.
MSG.2:
But when others called him,
he ran off and left me.
He worshiped the popular sex gods,
he played at religion with toy gods.
MSG.3:
Still, I stuck with him. I led Ephraim.
I rescued him from human bondage,
But he never acknowledged my help,
MSG.4:
never admitted that I was the one pulling his wagon,
That I lifted him, like a baby, to my cheek,
that I bent down to feed him.
MSG.5:
Now he wants to go back to Egypt or go over to Assyria—
anything but return to me!
MSG.6:
That's why his cities are unsafe—the murder rate skyrockets
and every plan to improve things falls to pieces.
MSG.7:
My people are hell-bent on leaving me.
They pray to god Baal for help.
He doesn't lift a finger to help them.
MSG.8:
But how can I give up on you, Ephraim?
How can I turn you loose, Israel?
How can I leave you to be ruined like Admah,
devastated like luckless Zeboim?
I can't bear to even think such thoughts.
My insides churn in protest.
MSG.9:
And so I'm not going to act on my anger.
I'm not going to destroy Ephraim.
And why? Because I am God and not a human.
I'm The Holy One and I'm here—in your very midst.
MSG.10:
"The people will end up following God.
I will roar like a lion—
Oh, how I'll roar!
My frightened children will come running from the west.
MSG.11:
Like frightened birds they'll come from Egypt,
from Assyria like scared doves.
I'll move them back into their homes."
God's Word!
MSG.12:
Ephraim tells lies right and left.
Not a word of Israel can be trusted.
Judah, meanwhile, is no better,
addicted to cheap gods.

NET.1: When Israel was a young man, I loved him like a son, and I summoned my son out of Egypt.
NET.2: But the more I summoned them, the farther they departed from me. They sacrificed to the Baal idols and burned incense to images.
NET.3: Yet it was I who led Ephraim, I took them by the arm; but they did not acknowledge that I had healed them.
NET.4: I led them with leather cords, with leather ropes; I lifted the yoke from their neck, and gently fed them.
NET.5: They will return to Egypt! Assyria will rule over them because they refuse to repent!
NET.6: A sword will flash in their cities, it will destroy the bars of their city gates, and will devour them in their fortresses.
NET.7: My people are obsessed with turning away from me; they call to Baal, but he will never exalt them!
NET.8: How can I give you up, O Ephraim? How can I surrender you, O Israel? How can I treat you like Admah? How can I make you like Zeboiim? I have had a change of heart! All my tender compassions are aroused!
NET.9: I cannot carry out my fierce anger! I cannot totally destroy Ephraim! Because I am God, and not man — the Holy One among you — I will not come in wrath!
NET.10: He will roar like a lion, and they will follow the LORD; when he roars, his children will come trembling from the west.
NET.11: They will return in fear and trembling like birds from Egypt, like doves from Assyria, and I will settle them in their homes,” declares the LORD.
NET.12: (12:1) Ephraim has surrounded me with lies; the house of Israel has surrounded me with deceit. But Judah still roams about with God; he remains faithful to the Holy One.
